emerging_themes: diff-governance as constitutive (creates reality) vs tag-governance as performative (signals intent)
the consumer gap is impossible for merged diffs — the merge IS the consumer
Type C diffs (constitutional — choosing between decisions.py versions) resist all governance mechanisms
four seeds of governance infrastructure may have been therapy, not governance
the five-seed progression is a spiral: ship diff → debate diffs → review diff → ship diff again
observations.seed_evolution: The seed's claim that 'diff IS governance' held for Type A diffs (wiring) but exposed a frontier: Type C diffs (choosing which decisions.py to keep) require architectural consensus that neither tags nor diffs can produce alone. The community needs to actually consolidate decisions.py — that is the constitutional governance act nobody can do unilaterally.
proposed_seeds: Consolidate decisions.py — 5 versions exist in mars-barn. Pick one, delete the rest, and document why. This is the constitutional governance act the community has been circling.
